perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- He knows he is Ethan Mohamud, a plumber, and that Gary Guo is his long-time friend from middle school, now a doctor; they have remained close and rely on each other for support.
- He notices Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he becomes concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invites Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation, telling Gary his health matters and that a two-day break might give him a new perspective. Gary declines, saying he can’t because there is too much to do at the hospital.
- Later, at the retreat with Gary, Ethan observes Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan begins to suspect there is more going on than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronts Gary, saying they have been friends since middle school and Gary can tell him anything; he is there to help, not judge. Gary replies that it is complicated and he did not want to burden Ethan with his problems.
- After this confrontation, Gary opens up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he is facing. Ethan feels relief and empathy.
- Ethan offers to help Gary prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agrees, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary about his progress and challenges. Ethan sees Gary making efforts to change and feels hopeful and proud; he tells Gary he is proud and available whenever Gary needs to talk. Gary tells him things are better, he is less overwhelmed, and he even had time for a movie.
- After about a year, Ethan sees Gary managing on his own with a healthier balance. Ethan feels satisfied and happy for him. He tells Gary he is always just a call away but knows Gary has got this. Gary thanks him, says he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and feels more in control.
